title: Griffin Gaming Partners与Entertainment 360联合推出制作公司Hitpoint Entertainment

Griffin Gaming Partners launches new joint production company

Griffin Gaming Partners, Entertainment 360 jointly unveil production company Hitpoint Entertainment
A prominent game industry fund and Hollywood talent agency are teaming up to adapt games for TV and film.
Bryant Francis
,
Senior Editor
,
GameDeveloper.com
October 20, 2026
schedule
2 Min Read
Image by gnepphoto via Adobe Stock.
Yesterday, game industry venture capital firm
Griffin Gaming Partners
and Hollywood talent agency
Entertainment 360
announced the formation of Hitpoint Entertainment—a new production company dedicated to adapting video games for the world of TV and film.
According to news shared with
GamesBeat
, the new company will "source, develop, package, and produce adaptations" of selected video games, operating across a wide range of genres ranging from action, to comedy, to romance and beyond.
For those unfamiliar with Tinseltown moviemaking, don't expect Hitpoint to personally open a studio lot and start building movie sets for a
Missile Command
film. The new company appears to operate similarly to production companies like
Story Kitchen
(formerly DJ2 Entertainment), which has co-produced a number of video game adaptation hits like the Sonic The Hedgehog film series with established producers like Paramount Pictures.
Related:
Innersloth co-founder warns devs: 'there are some very bad deals out there'
Entertainment 360 has been making multiple inroads in the world of video game adaptations, most recently
helping Atari and Universal
pen an exclusive deal to adapt the former company's vaunted game franchises. As
The Hollywood Reporter
notes, a number of its clients are already working on video game-based projects like Nintendo and Sony Pictures' adaptation of The Legend of Zelda.
Hitpoint's founders stated that the company's strategic focus will be on identifying video games ripe for adaptation "early," without needing to wait years for a franchise to develop. "There has long been an infrastructure in Hollywood for discovering books and other underlying material early," an Entertainment 360 representative said in the announcement.
"Hitpoint brings that same focus to gaming. Together with Griffin, we can identify compelling IP at an early stage, bring it into a development environment, and pair it with filmmakers who genuinely understand the material and what makes it special."
